questions.stem: An adult human skeleton has how many bones?
questions.explanation: Adult — 206 bones. Infants start with ~270 bones; many fuse with age (e.g., the cranial plates, sacrum, coccyx). The smallest bone is the stapes in the middle ear (~3 mm); the largest and strongest is the femur (thigh bone). The tiny hyoid bone in the throat is the only bone in the body that does not articulate with any other.

questions.stem: The largest muscle in the human body is the:
questions.explanation: Gluteus maximus — the main muscle of each buttock — is the largest muscle by volume in the human body. Powers hip extension (standing up, climbing). The smallest muscle is the stapedius (in the middle ear, ~1 mm long). The strongest muscle by raw force is the masseter (jaw). The hardest-working muscle is the heart (beats ~100,000 times a day).

questions.stem: Red blood cells are produced chiefly in the:
questions.explanation: RBCs are produced in the red bone marrow (mainly of the sternum, vertebrae, ribs, pelvis) in adults — a process called erythropoiesis. In the foetus, the liver does this job for a while. The kidneys secrete erythropoietin (EPO), the hormone that signals marrow to produce more RBCs — abused by some endurance athletes for its performance-enhancing effect. The spleen mainly destroys old RBCs.

questions.stem: The normal human body temperature is typically given as:
questions.explanation: Classic 37 °C (98.6 °F) — the textbook normal, from Carl Wunderlich's 19th-century measurements. Modern studies show a small variation (36.1-37.2 °C range; averages have drifted slightly downward). Temperature is regulated by the hypothalamus. Fever is usually defined as > 38 °C. Hypothermia < 35 °C; hyperthermia > 40 °C can be life-threatening.

questions.stem: Which human sense organ contains receptor cells called 'rods' and 'cones'?
questions.explanation: Rods and cones are photoreceptor cells in the retina. Rods (~120 million) work in dim light, sense brightness only (no colour). Cones (~6-7 million) work in bright light, detect colour (three types — red, green, blue). The fovea — the small central pit of the retina — is packed with cones for sharp central vision. Colour-blindness is usually a defect in the cones.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: Femur — longest, heaviest and strongest single bone in the body; roughly 1/4 of adult height. It can withstand ~30× its weight in vertical load. Tibia (shin) is second-longest. Humerus is the longest bone in the upper limb. The spine is a column of 33 vertebrae, not a single bone.

questions.stem: The 'universal donor' blood group (can donate RBCs to any ABO-Rh group in an emergency) is:
questions.explanation: O negative has no A, B or Rh antigens on its RBCs, so the recipient's immune system finds nothing foreign to attack — allowing emergency transfusion to any ABO-Rh recipient. Conversely, AB positive is the universal recipient (has all antigens — its plasma has no antibodies against A, B or Rh). O positive is the most common Indian blood group (~37 %); AB negative is the rarest.
